messages:
acme_support: Hey @maya, customer ACME reports tool call failures when sending file paths from Windows. They pasted a PowerShell here-string and get a 400 from our /toolcall endpoint.

acme_support: Payload they sent (sanitized):
```json
{
  "tool": "convert_pdf",
  "args": {
    "path": "C:\\Users\\Bob\\Documents\\report.pdf",
    "options": ["ocr","flatten",],  // copied from editor with trailing comma
  },
}
```

acme_support: API error: 400 - "Invalid tool args: JSON parse error at position 123". Can we confirm whether this is client-side or our parser?

maya: Thanks — tagging @tony and @sam. Quick Q: did they set Content-Type: application/json? PowerShell paste often uses single quotes / here-strings which can produce unescaped backslashes.

tony: I repro'd locally. Sending that exact body via curl without additional escaping returns the 400 and server logs: 
```
runtime: parse_tool_args failed: unexpected token ',' at 2:45
stack: /srv/runtime/parser.js:128:12
```

tony: Looks like a trailing comma in the args array is the immediate culprit. But the customer says their client pasted this from an editor and didn't intentionally add a comma. Could be an editor auto-complete.

qa-erin: Noted another wrinkle: some Windows paths have backslashes which our logs sometimes show as double-escaped, and if the client used single-quoted JSON (e.g., '"..."'), our gateway may have treated it as a raw string and not application/json. We should validate both the content-type and raw body.

maya: Can you paste the exact curl you used to repro, @tony? Also include the raw request body capture if possible.

tony: Repro curl (failing):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tool":"convert_pdf","args":{"path":"C:\\Users\\Bob\\Documents\\report.pdf","options":["ocr","flatten",],},}'
```

tony: Remove trailing commas and it succeeds: the corrected payload is valid JSON.

acme_dev: (customer) we pasted from VSCode — it added the trailing comma when we had both options selected. We didn't realize. Any chance the API could tolerate trailing commas? Our client libs often send them.

sam: From eng-runtime: we currently rely on strict JSON.parse on the raw request body for tool args. That intentionally rejects trailing commas and comments. It's by design to avoid ambiguity in tool arg shapes. We could add a tolerant parser in the gateway but that risks silently accepting malformed inputs and hiding issues.

sam: Quick mitigation: return a clearer error code and message indicating "trailing comma" or "invalid JSON at X" rather than generic parse error. We can also add a one-off pre-parse lint step that checks for common mistakes (trailing commas, unescaped backslashes) and returns a friendly client-side suggestion.

maya: Can @tony prototype a small gateway lint that detects trailing commas and returns a 400 with a message like: "tool args malformed: trailing comma in array/object at line X"? That would reduce churn with support.

tony: Yep, I'll open a short-lived feature branch. If it's low risk, we can deploy to staging today. Also propose adding a note in the SDKs: stringify JSON via JSON.stringify and ensure using double quotes for keys/strings.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - Toolcall parse errors from Windows path / trailing commas. Linked logs: log-7c8a2f2. Assigned to @tony.

qa-erin: For the customer repro, also confirm whether they used a proxy or curl wrapper that might re-serialize the body (PowerShell's Invoke-RestMethod can do odd conversions). If they used pwsh, advise using -Body (converted via ConvertTo-Json) or set -ContentType 'application/json; charset=utf-8'.

sam: Long-term, discussion item for infra: allow a permissive parser behind a feature flag that normalizes common mistakes, but keep strictness for audits/Security. I'll add to the eng-runtime backlog (ticket ENG-RN-412).

maya: Action items:
- @tony: open branch with pre-parse lint + staging deploy (ETA EOD).
- @sam: add backlog ticket + eng-runtime design note.
- @qa-erin: add unit tests for raw backslash handling and pwsh examples.
- @acme_support/@acme_dev: try removing trailing commas or using JSON.stringify; temporary workaround instructions provided below.

maya: Workaround (for customer): in PowerShell:
```powershell
$body = @{ tool = 'convert_pdf'; args = @{ path = 'C:\\Users\\Bob\\Documents\\report.pdf'; options = @('ocr','flatten') } } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/toolcall' -Method Post -ContentType 'application/json' -Body $body -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:TOKEN" }
```

acme_dev: Tried the PowerShell example — success! No 400 now. Thanks for the quick turnaround. :tada:

maya: Great, closing the customer loop. @tony please post PR link and I'll verify staging logs after deploy.

tony: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/561 — small pre-parse linter. Will deploy to staging after reviews.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll update the support ticket and mark as escalated -> resolved once staging is green.
